component.name: Iridia
component.summary: Set RGB lights from the colours of your wallpaper

description.p: Iridia takes the colours of your wallpaper and puts them on your RGB devices (LED strips, RAM, keyboards, fans and so on) through OpenRGB. Change the wallpaper and the lights follow.

ul.li: Finds the wallpaper on GNOME, KDE Plasma, XFCE, Cinnamon, MATE, COSMIC, Hyprland, Sway, niri and more
A pattern, brightness and colours for each zone; strips can be split into parts
Animations in the wallpaper's colours, and a map of the room they run across
Sensor bars for CPU temperature, load and memory
Follows the monitor's brightness, dims at night, goes off when the screen locks or the PC sleeps
Flashes chosen LEDs when a desktop notification comes in
WS2812B, WS2811, 12V RGB and RGBW strips, with colour order and colour correction
Keyboard shortcuts and saved setups through the iridia command
Favourites cards fit what's on them: wide cards use two columns, no empty band at the bottom
Arranging Favourites is easier, and cards keep their size
A card's colour ring shows what its strips really show
A dot on Updates when there's a new version
Everything counts as controlled while any strip is
The update notification goes away by itself again
Keyboard focus is visible, and rows and colours work from the keyboard
Clearer power buttons and lighter small text
Brightness slider on Home, Undo when hiding a strip, a list of keyboard shortcuts

description.p: A new look for the window.

ul.li: Home brings Status and Favourites together, glowing in your lights' colours
A side rail instead of a row of tabs
Devices as a compact, grouped list with brightness and power on each row
Strips glow on the Layout map; quieter colours and shorter texts throughout
Material 3 Expressive shapes and smooth motion
Text in the window can be selected and copied
Strips hidden on the Devices tab stay out of the Layout tab
One-click updates for the Arch, .deb and .rpm packages
Update now button on the new-version notification
The window uses less CPU while it sits open
The window shrinks again with Favourites open, and the cards follow its width
A card's brightness shows what the strips really show
Window buttons off by default on tiling compositors
Favourites cards: a card with only a few switches shows each across its full width, names in full
Favourites cards: every setting is a row with its name and a switch, laid out for each card size
A card's brightness slider shows and sets the real brightness, also while following the monitor
System packages for Arch, Debian and Ubuntu, and Fedora and openSUSE, on each release
Each strip: a switch for whether Iridia controls it, and a round power button
Favourites cards: a simpler editor, effect speed and scene switches, and every control shows
Favourites: cards with the controls you choose, on a grid you arrange, and one-tap looks
Scenes: make as many as you like, each for some strips, when something is fullscreen or an app is in front
Hide strips you don't use
Philips WiZ and Govee lights on the network, next to what OpenRGB drives, also on another VLAN
Per device: let Iridia control it, on its own, and for network lights only when you change it
Scenes: a different look for the lights while a game or a film is fullscreen, or for an app
Iridia needs Python 3.10 or newer
Notification flashes on the Layout tab, from A to B, with more effects and settings, in their own tab
The wallpaper is found on KDE Plasma installed next to Hyprland
The LEDs light back up fully after unlocking
Button text keeps the right size after changing the window size
Chosen LEDs flash when a desktop notification comes in
Sensor bars can fill from the middle
No cut-off text at the Default window size
Buttons no longer grow on hover; button groups light up on hover
Sensor bars work with colour correction
Numbered menus in the installer
ddcutil can be installed from the window
Colours reach the strips without a nudge
OpenRGB's server no longer restarts over and over
Devices show up sooner after OpenRGB starts
Pick the monitor whose brightness the LEDs follow
Devices found later are picked up; KDE's default wallpaper is found
Updates from the window, with a way back
Sensors, lock and idle, window sizes
Strips can be split into parts, and single LEDs set
Iridia's own OpenRGB client: one connection, every update confirmed
Seven animated effects, which can follow the layout of the room
OpenRGB starts reliably at login
Iridia starts OpenRGB's server itself
British spelling in the window by default
The first public release
